# Evidence
- Problem class: go-test-hang-unbounded-exec-build
- Model: openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash
- Solved: 2026-10-23T03:06:41.463Z
- Verification: solution produced by pi in sandbox; see signatures.json

signatures.description:
Symptom: a Go package's test binary sits at 0% CPU and the suite never reports a result; `go test -timeout=Ns ./pkg` is the only way to see it, and its stack dump points at a test helper shelling out to `go build` with no context.

Root cause: test helpers that rebuild the binary-under-test per test via exec.Command("go","build",...).CombinedOutput() with no exec.CommandContext and no timeout. On a loaded shared host the nested go build waits on build-cache/CPU contention indefinitely, so the OUTER package timeout is the only bound (25m in CI) and it reports a whole-package FAIL with no diagnostic.

Fix pattern: (1) build the binary once in TestMain (or sync.Once) and share the path; (2) run every external command under exec.CommandContext with a bounded timeout (<=60s) that t.Fatalf's the command line + captured output; (3) add a guard test that greps *_test.go for `exec.Command("go")` outside TestMain so the pattern cannot return.

Verification: the same package passed in 168s under the judge once host load dropped, proving the hang is environmental amplification of an unbounded wait, not a logic bug.
signatures.environment: go1.26.9 linux/amd64, shared host under load avg 33 (sibling CI battery), GOCACHE shared
